A stock balance (stock.quant) holds the on-hand and reserved quantity of one key: company, product, exact location, and optionally lot, package and owner. Balances are a projection of the stock ledger (ADR 0079, ADR 0139). Only one path writes them: erp_addon_stock::apply_quant_changes. Generic ORM writes of a balance are refused by name. Open move lines are the first caller: each holds its reservation on its quant key (see [Move lines](#move-lines)). Move validation and inventory application are later slices.

All items are re-exported at the crate root of erp-addon-stock. | Item | What it does | |---|---| | QuantKey | The six key parts. The company is the ledger line's company, never derived from the location. Build it with QuantKey::new(company, product, location) and .lot_id(..), .package_id(..), .owner_id(..). | | QuantChange | A signed on-hand delta, a signed reserved delta and the incoming date the stock carries: QuantChange::new(key, quantity, reserved), .in_date(..). | | apply_quant_changes(tx, &[QuantChange]) | Applies a batch in the caller's transaction and returns the new balances, one per distinct stored key, in lock order. One call takes at most 2,000 distinct keys and 32,000 changes. | | quant_engine::apply_quant_changes_in_chunks(tx, &[QuantChange]) | The same for a unit whose changes may exceed that bound: sorted by key and applied in ascending calls under the bound, every change of one key in the same call, so the lock order holds. The calls run in one savepoint, so a refusal in a later call undoes the earlier ones and the transaction can go on. Validation, cancellation and every reservation path (Check availability, a reservation at confirmation, a line create or write, Unreserve) use it. | | QuantFilter | Which balances a read covers: broad (the location and its descendants) or strict (exact key parts): QuantFilter::new(company, product, location), then .strict(..), .tracked(..) and the part setters. | | gather_quants(tx, &QuantFilter) | The matching balances, lot-bearing ones first, then by id. One query. | | available_quantity(tx, &QuantFilter, allow_negative) | Free quantity of the filter. One query. | | QuantError | Every refusal, with its message and error kind. | apply_quant_changes needs a REPEATABLE READ transaction, the ORM default. Use the native run_quant_unit entry below for a complete stock unit, including its probe and document changes. The ordinary Orm::run retries serialization failures but does not retry stock lock timeouts. Before it writes, a batch is checked as a whole. It is refused with nothing changed when: - a change has neither quantity nor reserved quantity; - a delta has more decimal digits than the Product Unit precision; - the product is not storable, the location is a view, or the lot belongs to another product; - the product, location, lot or owner belongs to another company than the key (a location of a parent company is accepted); - the company, product, location, lot, package or owner does not exist (a defect of the caller); - a release would take the reserved counter below zero. This is a defect of the caller and is reported, never clamped. The engine reads by SQL. Pending ORM writes of the transaction (a location usage written just before, a storable flag) are flushed before the checks, so the batch is checked against them. A key another transaction deleted after this one started is answered as a serialization failure (40001), which Orm::run retries. Changes at supplier, customer, inventory adjustment and production locations are accepted and store nothing: those balances live in the ledger only. A key whose quantity and reservation reach zero is deleted, unless it has a counted quantity or an assigned user. The incoming date of a key is the earliest of its own date (while it holds positive stock) and the dates its changes carry. With neither, it is the time of the call.

run_quant_unit(orm, unit, work) runs a repeatable async callback in a fresh transaction on every eligible retry. Build QuantUnit::new(principal, operation_identity, product_label) with a label that the caller is authorized to see, and use .context(context) when needed. The entry takes its policy snapshot once and keeps the same identity and inputs across attempts. The callback includes the availability probe, document changes and quant changes. It may be called again: keep external effects outside it and register post-commit effects with tx.after_commit. Do not commit manually. The entry owns the whole transaction and refuses a surrounding ORM or RPC unit before reading policy. It is a native entry point, not an RPC method. Serialization failures and deadlocks retry the entire callback. A lock timeout retries only when the ORM classified it as such; a NOWAIT refusal does not. Exhaustion returns QuantRetryExhausted, with a Lock error kind, the product label and actual attempt count. Access, validation and programming refusals are terminal. An uncertain commit result is terminal: inspect the operation's durable idempotency state before retrying it. Operation identity supplies correlation, not durable deduplication; the caller owns that protocol. The engine's apply_quant_changes entry still borrows a transaction and never retries or commits on its own. Negative-stock policy changes use their separate policy-unit contract.

The engine nets the changes of one call per key. It then sorts the keys ascending over (company, product, location, lot, package, owner), with an absent part after every present one (PostgreSQL's ASC NULLS LAST). It locks them in that order in one statement, inserting a zero row for a key that does not exist yet. Two calls over overlapping keys therefore never wait on each other in opposite orders. The order holds across calls only under one rule: **one engine call per unit of work**, or later calls only with keys above the highest key the transaction already holds. Collect the changes of a unit of work and pass them in one call. The engine keeps the keys each transaction locked; a later call that names a lower key it does not hold yet is refused before any lock, as a Programming error naming both keys. A key the transaction already holds may come again in any order. A key locked inside a savepoint that was rolled back is no longer held, because the rollback released its row lock; the engine notices the rollback and treats such a key as new. Count-state writes through the generic write lock in row order; make them before the engine call or in their own unit of work. Quant keys come third in the lock hierarchy of ADR 0079 D4.1. A caller locks its picking, move and policy rows before it calls the engine, and cost keys after.

| Product | allow_negative = false | allow_negative = true | |---|---|---| | Untracked | the signed sum of on hand minus reserved, at least zero | the signed sum | | Tracked (QuantFilter.tracked) | the sum of each lot's free quantity that is positive | the signed sum | A broad filter with a lot also counts stock without a lot. A strict tracked filter with a lot does not. The product's tracking mode is a field added by the lot work (planned); until then the caller states it in the filter.

The engine checks no model access or record rule, as an internal service. The transition that calls it has already checked access on its own documents. The engine is never an RPC method. On stock.quant: - create is refused, after the model access check (so a user without access still gets the access refusal); - write of a key part, quantity, reserved_quantity or in_date is refused, naming the field's label; the counted quantity and the assigned user stay writable; - copy is refused, after the create access check; - the generic upsert by the declared key is refused, after the create and write access checks (it would run no create or write override); - unlink runs the model access check, then refuses a quant with an on-hand or reserved quantity for every caller, the superuser too. Deleting a zero quant requires the caller's unlink access and record rules to allow it. The engine deletes its own zero keys. These refusals are user errors whose message says that balances change only through stock moves and inventory adjustments; the client's New and Duplicate buttons can reach them. On stock.move and stock.move.line, the done time, and on lines also the membership and the correction counter, are written only by the stock engine: a create or write that names one of them is refused for every caller, after the model access check, with a user error naming the field's label. Correction rows (stock.move.line.correction) and serial positions (stock.serial.position) are read only for stock users and managers; only the engine writes them. available_quantity is a read-only PostgreSQL virtual generated column for on hand minus reserved. It answers row reads and available_quantity:sum from the same exact signed expression, including stock received or reserved before the catalog upgrade. It stores no second balance. The grouped read of inventory_quantity_auto_apply follows quantity; generic callers cannot write a balance through that alias. A quant's display name identifies its location, followed by each present lot, package and owner. The default on_hand filter follows visible active warehouses for the selected companies. The contexts warehouse_id and location (also search_warehouse, search_location) accept positive IDs or lists of IDs. With an explicit location, strict chooses that location only. Warehouse and location names in those context values require resolution to IDs before submitting the filter. Searching custom properties of a lot remains dependent on the lot-properties field on stock lots.

A location write is refused when: - it changes the company of a location (archive it and create a new one instead); - it makes a location holding any balance a view; - it changes the usage of a location holding any non-zero on-hand or reserved quantity. The reference blocks only positive stock; here a negative or reserved-only balance blocks too, because a balance at a virtual usage is never stored and would stay frozen there; - it archives a location whose internal locations (itself or below) hold stock. The checks also catch values that convert to a change: an active value other than true (null or 0 from RPC, an empty or integer cell from Rust) is checked as an archive, and a usage value that is not a usage name is checked as a usage change. Pending ORM writes (a child moved to another parent just before) are flushed before the checks read. Concurrent stock changes. The engine takes a share lock on the locations of its keys. A location guard locks the locations it decides on (for an archive, every location below too) without waiting: - while a stock change at those locations is still open, the guard fails as a serialization failure and Orm::run retries it; once the change committed, the retry sees its balance; - a stock change that starts after the guard waits for the guard's transaction, is then retried, and sees the new usage or archive. The tracking check locks the product rows in the same way, so an open insert of a lot, line or quant of the product retries it. Not covered yet: a stock change that committed after the guard's transaction began and before the guard's lock. The guard's snapshot does not show it and no lock is left to meet, so the guard decides without it. Closing that needs the rule as a database constraint that is checked across snapshots.

The native unit's limits are declared technical system parameters of stock (ADR 0227), in **Technical, System Parameters**, not on the Settings page. Only system administrators read and change them there; the unit reads them itself (erp_sdk::params::get_int, elevated), so every caller of a stock unit has them applied. Each new invocation reads committed policy; a save does not extend an invocation already in progress. A stored text outside its declaration fails the invocation with Stored parameter <key> is invalid. before any work. Negative stock is allowed. The switch that forbids it per location is the location policy's forbid_negative field. For a flagged location, apply_quant_changes checks the locked on-hand of each key after netting: a change that lowers it below zero fails with QuantError::NegativeStockForbidden (kind Validation, before any write, never clamped); a change that only repays an existing deficit, and every unflagged location, behave as before. Switching the flag on is refused with ForbidNegativeBlocked while a key at the location is below zero or has more reserved than on hand. A switch that meets an open stock change at the location, or one that took a key's free quantity (on hand minus reserved) below zero after the switch's transaction began, fails as a serialization failure and Orm::run retries it on a snapshot that sees the balance. The engine marks the location's policy row only when a key crosses from a free quantity at or above zero to one below it; a further change of a key that is below zero already writes nothing, because the switch sees that key in its snapshot. Each mark makes the other engine calls at that location whose snapshot is older fail once with a retryable serialization failure, and two calls that both cross at one location can deadlock (one is retried). Not delivered yet: reservation re-flooring. The decimal precision is the Product Unit precision (Settings, Technical, Decimal Accuracy). Every key below begins with stock.quant_. Zero is refused, not treated as unlimited; an empty or deleted row means the default. | Key suffix | Default | Allowed range | |---|---:|---:| | lock_timeout_ms | 1000 ms | 10–10000 ms | | max_attempts | 5 | 1–5 | | retry_base_ms | 50 ms | 1–2000 ms | | retry_cap_ms | 2000 ms | 1–10000 ms | | idle_transaction_timeout_ms | 60000 ms | 1000–600000 ms | | tcp_keepalives_idle_s | 30 s | 1–300 s | | tcp_keepalives_interval_s | 10 s | 1–60 s | | tcp_keepalives_count | 3 | 1–10 | The retry base cannot exceed its cap (parameter group stock.quant_retry_backoff). The lock timeout must be below the transaction's effective statement limit; incompatible values refuse the invocation before business work. Idle-session and TCP keepalive values apply locally to each transaction. Defaults are operational choices; performance calibration is deferred. Before stock 1.5 these keys were global Settings values. The 1.5 upgrade moves each stored value to the parameter of the same key (ADR 0227 §7): the Settings revision does not change, a parameter row that already held another text is replaced by the Settings value and audited with actor migration:stock@1.5, and a stored value outside its range stops the upgrade naming the key. The old rows stay in place, unread, for one release.

An open, active stock.move.line of a storable product reserves its product-unit quantity on its key (company, product, its source location, lot, package, owner). The line overrides of the stock addon keep that true for ORM and RPC callers alike: - create takes the move's transfer, company, product, locations, unit and picked flag when they are not given, stamps the product-unit snapshot from the unit service, locks the move's transfer and the move, inserts, and raises the reserved quantity of each new line's key; - write of the quantity, unit, source location, package or owner releases the old reservation and takes the new one, netted per key in one engine call, also when the written lines need different unit snapshots; the move, transfer, company and product of a line cannot change; - unlink gives the reservation back. After each of them one statement sets every touched move's quantity (the sum of its active lines in the move's unit) and bumps open_line_version, and one recomputes the move's state (covered demand assigned, partly covered partially_available, otherwise confirmed, or waiting behind open origins). The transfer's counters and state follow from the move counter triggers. These statements, confirmation and reservation are the only writers of a move's state and quantity: a create or write naming either, for any caller and also through a transfer's move_ids commands, is refused with StockError::DerivedFromLines, as is a default_state or default_quantity context key on a move create; a new or copied move starts draft with no quantity. A source location that bypasses reservation (vendor, customer, inventory, production) and a product that does not track inventory store no reservation. Lots on lines and lines without a move are refused by name until their slices exist, also when the lot comes as a default_lot_id, default_lot_name or default_child_mode context key; done lines are fixed (see [Validation](#validation)). A create checks that the caller may read the moves it names before it locks them. The lines that Check Availability and validation create themselves never take the caller's default_* context.

stock.picking has two methods (also RPC, effect = write): - action_assign (Check Availability) reserves the transfer's open moves, refused by name when there is none. It locks the transfers and all their moves once, confirms the drafts without reserving, and reserves every open move in one engine call. A move from a location that bypasses reservation, or of a product that keeps no stock, gets one line for its whole missing quantity. A make-to-order move without origins waits; a move with origin moves keeps its state until chained reservation exists. Every other move takes free, lot-less stock (on hand minus reserved) from its source location and the locations below it, oldest incoming date first, as one line per key, growing an unpicked line of the same key. The quantity is converted to the move's unit rounding down, so a line never takes more than is free. - do_unreserve deletes the unpicked lines of moves that are not picked, done or cancelled; a done move is refused. Concurrency follows ADR 0139 D2: the free stock is read once without a lock (the probe), then the chosen keys are locked in key order by one engine call whose changes are marked with QuantChange::as_probed. A key another unit changed after the probe fails the unit with a retryable 40001 (from the lock, or QuantError::ChangedSinceProbe from the floor), and the retry probes again, so a reservation is short only when the probe found less, never because of a lock. At a location whose policy forbids negative stock, every growing reservation, an explicit line edit included, is refused with QuantError::ReservationExceedsFree when it would take more than is free; elsewhere an explicit line may over-reserve, as in the reference.

stock.picking.action_confirm (RPC, effect = write) confirms a transfer's draft moves in one statement: a move with origin moves becomes waiting, any other confirmed, and a move whose operation type reserves at confirmation gets today's reservation date. The confirmed moves that are returns, bypass reservation, reserve at confirmation or whose reservation date has come are then reserved as by action_assign, in the same unit of work. A transfer without a draft move is refused by name. A make-to-order move (or one whose rule falls back to an order) is refused until the procurement engine exists. action_assign confirms draft transfers first. A new move that names a transfer (or has default_picking_id in the context) takes the transfer's company, source, destination, operation type and contact when its values do not name them, so a client sends only the product and the demand; the product's unit is filled the same way (and proposed by the product_id onchange). The transfer's values are read after the ORM's pending writes are flushed, so a row added in the same save that changes the transfer's header takes the new header.

stock.picking.button_validate (Validate, RPC, effect = write) completes confirmed, waiting or ready transfers. It locks the transfers, then their open moves, and refuses by name: only done transfers, a cancelled transfer, a transfer without moves, and one whose moves carry no quantity. A draft transfer is confirmed on the way (without the early reservation, since the unit makes one engine call) and each of its moves without quantity gets one line for its demand at its own locations; a quantity entered before is kept. Those lines were never reserved: their source keys go to the engine as QuantChange::as_floored, so at a location that forbids negative stock a take that would use stock reserved for other transfers is refused with ReservationExceedsFree and nothing changes (ADR 0139 D6.3); elsewhere it is taken. When no move is picked every move is taken as picked. A move short of its demand (or an unpicked move with demand) would need a backorder and is refused by name, unless the operation type never creates backorders: then the move is done with its quantity and the unpicked or empty moves are cancelled. A move without quantity and without demand is cancelled; cancelling a move that feeds an open move is refused. The stock then changes in **one engine call** per validation (in ascending calls of at most 2,000 keys when the validation touches more): the reservations of the done and deleted lines are released and each done line's quantity leaves its source key and arrives at its destination key (the result package as package), netted per key and applied in the engine's key order. A location that forbids negative stock refuses the whole validation by name and nothing is written. Zero lines are deleted, the done lines join the ledger (membership = 'done', done_at), the moves become done with their completion time, and the transfer gets its done date; the transfer's counters and state follow from the move counter triggers, and the overview counts are notified. Two sessions validating one transfer: the later one fails with a retryable 40001 on the transfer lock, and its retry is refused because the transfer is done. Done work is fixed for every caller, sudo included (allow-lists in addons/stock/src/done.rs): a done move may still change only its description, origin, priority, sequence, deadline, chain links and references; a done transfer only its note, origin, responsible, printed and locked flags and priority. Every other field is refused by name, also as x2many commands. No move joins a done transfer (in the values or as default_picking_id), done moves and transfers are not deleted, and no create, write or default_state sets a move to done: Validate is the only way there. Not yet: backorders, lots, the line picked flag (every line of a done move is done), the incoming date carried from the source, re-flooring other reservations when a validation drives free stock negative at an unflagged location, and assigning the destination moves of a chain.

- A new transfer without a reference (none, empty or the default /, and no default_name in the context) draws the next number of its operation type's sequence (erp_sdk::sequence::draw_by_id); a type without a sequence leaves /. Its source, destination and company come from the operation type when the values and the context defaults do not name them; on the form the picking_type_id onchange proposes the same. - action_cancel (Cancel, RPC, effect = write) cancels the open moves of the transfers: their open lines are deleted and their reservations given back in one engine call, the moves become cancel, unpicked and make-to-stock, and the transfers are locked (is_locked). A done transfer and a transfer without moves are refused by name (an empty transfer is a draft by its counters: delete it); a move that feeds an open move is refused until cancel propagation exists. - Deleting a transfer cancels its open moves, deletes all its moves through the move model, then the transfer; a done transfer is refused.

Later quant slices add: - serial positions and the one-serial-per-location rule, after the lot work (planned); - compensation of lot-less negative stock when lots arrive; - searching quants by a custom property of the lot, when product and lot records provide property definitions; - relocating or repacking balances. Removal strategies and applying a counted quantity through the inventory workflow are separate deliveries.

**Proposal; acceptance and implementation are pending.** The service, fields and projection lifecycle on this page are not available yet. There is no setup command or executable API example for this proposal.

The proposed native stock service accepts a validated batch of products, companies, warehouse/location scope, optional dates and dimensions in the caller's transaction. It returns exact on-hand, reserved, incoming, outgoing, free and forecast quantities, plus units and a result identity. Addons consume the service rather than querying its projection tables or maintaining a second supply/demand total. Stock accounting keeps ownership of values; a quantity result is not a valuation approval. Explicit empty scope means zero for permitted products; an empty product list returns an empty batch. Absence of company selection uses the environment's allowed companies. Forbidden explicit companies or locations fail access checks. Warehouse unions classify movements once: a transfer inside the union is neither incoming nor outgoing. Overlapping roots do not duplicate quantities. Legacy context adaptation remains separate from the typed boundary. Location and warehouse name matching keeps substring behavior, with warnings containing only authorized candidates. Strict-name matching is opt-in. Unknown options and invalid types fail; they do not choose a broader default scope.

Lot, owner and package restrictions have different meanings for physical stock and open moves. Package filters constrain current quant quantities, not planned move supply. A lot filter counts each qualifying open move once. Nullable owner selectors distinguish unrestricted, ownerless and named owners; an empty legacy owners set means ownerless, not every owner. Past product-field quantities reconstruct exact historical on-hand while reporting **current** reservations. Results label this reservation basis. Historical reservation, lot/package attribution, expiry and warehouse-topology reconstruction are unsupported in the first proposed version. They return an explicit error; a daily checkpoint cannot silently answer a question it lacks the dimensions to cover. Date-only boundaries use UTC days; timestamp queries preserve intraday precision. Backdated movements and corrections can change a later query for an old business date. Sparse checkpoints accelerate the complete ledger fold and cannot replace missing history with zero. Removing acceleration data does not delete source facts.

Every contributing source must satisfy current model, field, company and record access. A company-filtered total is insufficient when record rules distinguish rows within it. The service uses a declared exact-source plan or refuses an unsupported request when aggregate grain cannot preserve visibility. Operational decisions and post-write product blocks use primary transactions. Analytical browsing may use a bounded-lag replica with visible route and freshness information. Unknown lag is not a fresh result. The service cannot upgrade an already-open replica transaction secretly; the caller must select the required consistency before opening it. Quantity payloads belong to an authorized transaction or report run. Changes to principal, elevation, companies, policy, options or generations require a new identity and authorization decision. Addons must not reuse an earlier quantity payload merely because its products and company IDs match.

Forecast display pages contain at most 200 lines, while reconciliation covers the entire admitted demand universe. A refreshed load-more prefix replaces the old prefix and totals together; it cannot append rows from a new snapshot to old totals. Large requests fail a declared limit or use a durable report workflow. Default-scope search, sort and group use the same rounded measures displayed on product fields, including zero for authorized products without stock rows. Extensions for expiry, rental or subscription demand must declare their semantics and version. Missing required providers, unknown options, overflow and exceeded budgets fail with explicit error kinds and messages. Providers cannot relax authorization or admission limits. The legacy quantity-report model name is not a general addon compatibility promise.

No migration, default record or background job is installed by this design proposal. Future installation must build and validate projection generations before marking them ready. An unavailable generation must use an admitted exact-source plan or fail visibly; missing initialization is not empty stock. Maintenance will use bounded, fenced jobs with explicit source-equivalence checks. Opening a report will not start an unbounded repair or replay. Operational commands and runtime examples will accompany the implementation slices.

Developer page for the tracking conversion check. The decision lives in erp_addon_stock::tracking; the product's tracking field and its write path belong to the lot work (planned), which calls it.

use erp_addon_stock::tracking::{Tracking, TrackingChange, check_tracking_change}; check_tracking_change(tx, &[TrackingChange { product_id, from: Tracking::Serial, to: Tracking::Lot }]).await?; Call it from the write path of tracking, in the transaction of the write, with every product the write touches (one call per write, not one per product: it runs one query per kind for the whole batch). A refusal is a Validation error; the write rolls back with the transaction. Tracking::from_selection reads the stored selection (empty is untracked) and refuses any other value.

| From | To | Result | |---|---|---| | any | the same | allowed | | untracked | lot | allowed; stock already on hand stays without a lot (the client may show the reference's hint) | | lot | untracked | allowed; lots stay on their quants and lines | | serial | untracked, lot | refused while a serial number is on hand or on an open line | | lot, untracked | serial | refused while a lot is on hand or on an open line (checked on the new mode, so lot to untracked to serial cannot get round it) | Counted: serial positions and lot quants of non-zero quantity, open active lines (serial children, or plain lines naming a lot). Not counted: zero quantity rows, done lines, inactive children. A lot or serial number counts once however many rows name it. Cases: SPEC-STOCKLEDGER-031, -037, -038, SPEC-STOCKOPS-064. The refusal text is ADR 0139 D5.6's: it names the product, the number found and says that converting existing stock is not available yet. Words it from StockError::TrackingChangeBlocked, so a caller never builds its own sentence.

Converting the refused cases needs the writers of serial positions and open serial children (planned). No setting is involved: the decision has no threshold. The count is exact, not capped; it reads the rows of the named products only (unmeasured, DEFERRED_PERFORMANCE).
